income.description: WW:3G closing, Bradley Berry via Triad
income.note: Carried three weeks. One document outstanding from Bradley Berry, then closes autonomously through Triad.

Sale price $36,500 confirmed 8/27. Net roughly $30,000 after the $7,000 Vincent lien. GRP holds the title. Trent directed the excess proceeds be used to pay off the 2125 Patricia floor plan note, because PEP is slow to return titles.

Make ready completed, behind the Aug 10 target. Listed at $35,000 sale only. Inquiries but no applicants as of 8/27. Trent directed that WW:6D excess proceeds retire the floor plan note rather than waiting for this sale, because PEP takes two to four months to return a title.

Confirmed PENDING SALE on 9/2, still showing in the listing category in Rent Manager. Price raised to $30,000 on 8/27. Signed purchase agreement from Jessica Rehnquist, in financing. The Vincent lien is paid from buyer loan funding at closing, so it does not touch GRP cash.
Range $19,000 to $25,000. Trent noted on 8/27 that this one will take a little longer.
Bill of sale sent to Beth. Title transfer in process. Listing partially furnished. Trent flagged on 8/27 as further out.
Xochitl working a new Triad contact. Tenant still paying rent. Not counted on in the window.

Payoff quoted at $37,640.38, good through 9/30/26. Beth requested it from 21st Mortgage on 9/2; it is not available online. Tenant owned home conversion follows the payoff. Net effect on cash is not yet established, so it carries no amount.

expenses.note: New this week. $1,828.75 already paid through GRP across Clayton Evans, Kodey Gilpin and Joshuah Muse. Total scope not yet known.
Owed to Vincent once WW:6D sells. Tied to the closing date, which is not yet set.
Rico committed on 8/27 to finish 44 Waterway by end of that week. Confirmed almost done on 9/2, a month behind the Aug 15 target.
Started as of 9/2 after a capacity issue was resolved. Gilmore bid was rejected at $26,000; reverting to Rico at roughly $15,000. Completion still expected in Q4.
Demo is complete. To Do Property Cleanup sent the invoice to Beth on 8/26, after the submittal cutoff, so it lands on the following run. $3,500 confirmed by Trent on 8/20.
Payoff $37,640.38 good through 9/30/26. Precedes the tenant owned home conversion. No funding source or date decided, so it is excluded from the forecast.
Rico's next start after 44 Waterway. Mid September is the start date, not the target completion, so this one is behind. Amount not yet established.

floor_plan.note: Swearingen buyback. Promissory note dated 5/29/26, principal $27,687.48 at 16 percent, six month term, prepayable without penalty. Payoff shown includes accrued interest. Home listed 8/10 at $35,000; a sale before the repayment date retires the note and nets GRP roughly $5,100.
PEP loan 76499, borrower Melissa Harris, 61 days delinquent, payoff $30,842.02. Buyback confirmed as going to happen; will be placed on floor plan. No date set, so it is not in the forecast.

exposure.note: PEP loan 6359. Nearly paid off. Not a buyback concern; monitoring only.
PEP loan 75029. Largest delinquent balance on the roster. Monitoring.

portfolio.note: Total PEP payoff across the portfolio is $1.4 million as of 9/2, down from a little over $2 million at the start, through buybacks and not adding new loans. Seven Winterwood homes carry roughly $350,000 of that, with three close to $60,000 each.

notes.text: The forecast no longer goes short. Low point is $15,304 the week of 10/30. The WW:6D closing at $36,500 lands the week of 9/18 and carries the portfolio through October. Without it the last three weeks of October run negative.

October has five Thursdays, so the fourth week weighting is split across 10/23 and 10/30. Weekly timing comes from eight weeks of actual cash flow; levels come from the Fiscal Year Budget. Opening cash is the true bank balance of $86,283.

cfo_summary: Total available cash is $83,083 against a true bank balance of $86,283. Uncleared transactions are only $3,200, the cleanest position of the year. After $26,250 in external payments and $29,747 in intercompany management fees, projected end of week is $56,833. Twenty one bills, all approved.
September rent lifted available cash $40,561 in one week. Eight of nine entities improved. Four Seasons is the strongest position at $20,062 projected, followed by Countryside at $8,425.

GRP went negative again and the management fees are the only thing fixing it. Available opened at negative $9,851, down $16,248 from last week's positive $6,397. The $29,747 of fees bring it back to a projected $4,296. That is the fourth time in eleven weeks GRP has carried a negative balance, and the pattern is unchanged: GRP pays closing costs and rehab on behalf of the property entities and depends on the monthly fee sweep to recover.

Two management fees were reversed in the source file. RMF was entered at $5,235.60 and Winterwood at $703.80, against a history of roughly $800 for RMF and $5,000 for Winterwood. Corrected to RMF $703.80 and Winterwood $5,235.60. Total fees and the GRP deposit are unchanged; the correction moves $4,532 of pressure from RMF onto Winterwood.

Three entities finish thin. Group Group sits at $85 for the third straight week with no bills and no deposits. Riverside projects to $2,237 after $3,600 of Whitley tree removal, its second Whitley bill in three weeks totalling $8,100. Winterwood projects to $2,471 after $11,911, the heaviest run of any entity this week.

The forecast no longer goes short, bottoming at $15,304 on 10/30. The change is WW:6D, which now carries a confirmed sale price of $36,500 and lands the week of 9/18. Net of the $7,000 Vincent lien it puts roughly $30,000 into GRP. Without that closing the last three weeks of October run negative, so the whole October picture rests on one sale.

Trent directed that the WW:6D proceeds retire the 2125 Patricia floor plan note rather than waiting for that home to sell, because PEP takes two to four months to return a title. The note is $29,903 due November 29 against a $36,500 closing, so the sequencing works if 6D closes on time.

PEP exposure resolved in three of four cases this week. WW:11A is saved and off the board; the couple are staying and GRP is billing the roof and repairs back at $50 a month. Brian Miller at WW:6B is current with PEP and off the board. What remains is DA: 54, Melissa Harris, 61 days delinquent at a $30,842 payoff, which will be bought back and placed on floor plan. That takes floor plan from one home to two and roughly $60,700 total. RE: 11 at $3,184 and CP: 77 JPL at $47,512 are delinquent but monitoring only. Total PEP payoff across the portfolio is $1.4 million, down from a little over $2 million at the start.

The 9 Corey payoff is $37,640.38, good through 9/30/26. Beth requested it from 21st Mortgage on 9/2. It precedes the tenant owned home conversion. No funding source or date has been decided, so it is on the watchlist as Open and excluded from the forecast. If it is funded before month end it is the largest single discretionary outflow in the window.

Two watchlist decisions from the 8/27 review. 20 Powerline comes off the income side entirely; Mara offered $1,000 rather than the $10,000 carried, the home is full of fleas, roaches and bedbugs, and Justin asked that it be taken out of projected cash flow because he is not counting on it selling. FS2:056 was raised from $25,000 to $30,000. The FS1:23 demo is complete and the $3,500 invoice reached Beth on 8/26, after the submittal cutoff, so it lands on next week's run.

Three make ready items moved on 9/2. FS2:034 has started after the capacity issue was resolved and reverts to Rico at roughly $15,000 rather than the $26,000 Gilmore bid. FS1:15 is repaired and becomes Dalton's next rehab. FS2:046 and FS2:047 are Rico's next start at mid September, which is a start date rather than a completion target, so that pair is behind. 20 Powerline is confirmed as a rehabber sale and is off the income board entirely.

for_ownership.label: Projected end-of-week cash
for_ownership.paragraph: We close this week at roughly $56,800 available across all accounts. September rent landed and lifted cash by about $41,000, and nearly every account improved. Of the $56,000 in bills going out this week, $30,000 is the monthly management fee moving from the parks into Golden Rule Practices, which is what brings that account back from negative. Winterwood 6D is now under contract at $36,500 and should close in about two weeks, and the proceeds will pay off the Patricia floor plan note. With that sale the next sixty days are covered. Without it, the last three weeks of October come up short. Three accounts finish thin this week: Group Group at $85, Riverside at $2,200 and Winterwood at $2,500.
